summary: This note is a short biographical overview of Ercole Manfredi, an architect who advanced his career through the court of King Vajiravudh in Thailand. He left government service to work privately as Thailand's political change ended absolute monarchy and reduced government hiring of foreigners. By adopting a Thai identity, marrying a Thai woman and settling permanently, he stayed a respected figure in Thai architecture and later lectured at Chulalongkorn University. The note says his works span royal residences and public institutions in styles from Venetian Gothic to modernist, often incorporating Thai traditional elements, though no complete records of them were kept.
one_line: Biographical note on Ercole Manfredi, a foreign-born architect who worked at King Vajiravudh's court and later shaped Bangkok's architectural heritage.
